author: site-pw@local
body: Just say we are we're trying to find what predicts the, how strongly it marked the importance of a persona in terms of the persona itself. And we thought kind of that the cosine similarity from the assistant would do this but then it wasn't actually the case. So now we just tried JS divergence.

anchor.quote: Motivation: Two prior length-controlled tests (#340, #368) overturned the #271 claim that hidden-state cosine distance from the assistant centroid predicts how strongly a [ZLT] marker implants into a persona. After the 2026-05-22 mentor meeting I tried the same idea in output space instead of hidden-state space: maybe the predictor was right but the space was wrong.

addressed_note: Rewrote Motivation in plain language: we're trying to predict source rate from persona properties; thought cosine from the assistant would do it, #340/#368 overturned that, so we're trying JS divergence.

author: site-pw@local

anchor.quote: each persona's mean pairwise output-distance to the other 47 panel members (the secondary, "mean pairwise output-distance to other personas").

addressed_note: Rewrote the secondary predictor description in plain English: for each persona, compute the divergence to every other persona on the panel, then average across the 47 others.

author: site-pw@local

anchor.quote: Next steps: Three follow-ups worth queuing: test a behavioral judgment predictor (Claude-scored "how non-assistant does this persona feel") on the same panel; re-run the mean pairwise predictor on a panel with more variation outside the helpful-assistant family (the current interval barely excludes zero, and one length tercile alone trends in the predicted direction at n=22, worth a bigger panel and not a claim); pivot vulnerability prediction toward non-geometric predictors such as capability profile, training-data overlap of the source prompt's bag-of-words, or prompt-format prior.

addressed_note: Trimmed Next steps to a single 'open thread' line and dropped the three specific follow-up suggestions; spec requires the bullet so kept the label with a noncommittal summary.

author: site-pw@local

anchor.quote: The cosine-from-assistant axis (overturned in #340 / #368) rank-correlates strongly with the primary on the N=24 subset where both exist, so this is the same axis re-expressed, not independent evidence. See figure below.
